info.title: Security Incident Management API
info.description:
Platform for **security alerts, incidents, vulnerabilities, risk, remediation, investigations, playbooks, SLAs,
audit, notifications, dashboards and reports**.

### Authenticating in Swagger
1. Call `POST /api/v1/auth/login` (or press **Authorize** and enter e-mail as *username* + password).
2. Use the returned `access_token`; refresh with `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh`.

### Conventions
* Lists are paginated: `?page=1&size=20` and return `{items, total, page, size, pages}`.
* Errors share one envelope: `{"success": false, "error": {"code", "message", "details"}, "request_id"}`.
* Timestamps are ISO-8601 UTC. Playbook actions are **simulated** only. Audit logs are append-only.

post.description:
Self-registration. The account has **no role** and is **inactive** until an administrator activates it and
assigns a role (unless `REGISTRATION_AUTO_ACTIVATE=true`).
Returns a short-lived **access token** and a long-lived **refresh token**.

post.summary: Rotate tokens with a refresh token
post.description: Each refresh token can be used **once**. Re-using a rotated token revokes every session of the user.

post.summary: Log out and invalidate the tokens
post.description: Revokes the current session: both its access and refresh token stop working immediately.

detected within `DUPLICATE_ALERT_WINDOW_MINUTES` is stored with `is_duplicate=true` and `duplicate_of_id`
pointing at the original, whose `occurrence_count` is incremented (and severity raised if the repeat is more
severe).

false_positive; in_progress -> resolved | false_positive; resolved -> in_progress; false_positive -> new.

get.summary: Identify repeated alerts affecting the same asset
get.description:
Rule: alerts of the same category on the same asset, each detected within `window_minutes` of the previous
one, form a group; groups with at least `min_alerts` alerts are reported.

post.summary: Create an incident (from alerts, a correlation group, or manually)
post.description:
Severity defaults to the highest linked-alert severity; an SLA is attached automatically.

**Duplicate-incident rule:** if an *open* incident already exists for the same asset and category created within
`DUPLICATE_INCIDENT_WINDOW_HOURS`, the request is rejected with `409 duplicate_incident` unless
`allow_duplicate=true` (the new incident is then linked to the existing one as `possible_duplicate`).

Managers assign anyone; analysts can only claim an unassigned incident. The first assignment is the SLA

patch.description:
assigned -> investigating <-> containment; resolved -> investigating (re-open). Use `/resolve` to resolve and
the closure endpoints to close.

post.description: Four-eyes rule: the approver must be a different person from the one who requested the closure.
Re-opens the incident (`investigating`); a comment is required.
